problem: Prior surveys cover only one or two of vision, language and embodied AI (e.g. VIN, language-RL, multimodal ML). None gives a holistic view of vision-language embodied planning tasks that unifies navigation, question answering, object referral, dialogue and manipulation, or lays out the high-level challenges.
motivation: The number of vision-language embodied tasks and datasets has grown fast but they are studied in isolation, so it is hard to compare tasks, methods, metrics and simulators. Real-world deployment also needs generalisation, social interaction and dynamic environments, which current benchmarks largely ignore.
key_idea: Define Embodied Vision-Language Planning (EVLP) as a unified family of tasks (VLN, EQA, EOR, VDN, EGM), organise it in a taxonomy of tasks, approaches and evaluation, and use it to identify core open challenges.
insight: This is a survey with no experiments or ablations. Its main argument is that current EVLP work is fragmented across tasks and simulators, uses static dialogue and stationary environments, and relies on end-goal success metrics. Progress therefore needs cross-task benchmarks, more realistic simulators and datasets, domain and commonsense knowledge, and explicit generalisation tests. It cites Zhu et al. (2021b), where masking object or direction words changes performance little, as evidence that models may not truly ground language.
method: Problem formalisation: defines planning as a tuple of states, actions, initial and goal states, then defines EVLP with a state built from vision and language histories.
Task taxonomy: five tasks (VLN, EQA, EOR, VDN, EGM) compared by navigation, object identification, environment interaction and reasoning mode (Table 1).

Approach review: vision, language and multimodal modelling; planning via mapping/exploration, search/topological planning and hierarchical decomposition; supervised, RL and hybrid learning; data augmentation, auxiliary objectives, pre-training, multitask learning, reward shaping.

Evaluation review: metrics grouped into success, distance, path similarity, instruction fidelity and object selection (Tables 2-5), with a comparison of 17 simulators (Table 6) and 25 datasets (Table 7).
Open challenges: social interaction, dynamic environments, cross-task learning, domain knowledge (pre-training, commonsense), training objectives, and evaluation realness and generalisability.

setting.simulator: n/a (surveys Matterport3DSim, Habitat, AI2-THOR, StreetLearn and others)

numbers_note: Survey paper with no experimental results of its own.
results: There are no experimental results. Contributions are the EVLP taxonomy, comparison tables of metrics, simulators and datasets, and a set of core challenges: social interaction, dynamic environments, cross-task learning, domain knowledge, training objectives, and simulator and dataset realness with generalisation tests.
limitations: Scope is limited to single-agent, static environments, and real-world robotics issues (affordances, control) are excluded.
Coverage stops around 2021, so it predates large language model and foundation-model agents.
Descriptive rather than quantitative: no unified benchmark comparison of method performance.
